subtopics.title: The Scale from 0 to 1 and Three Ways to Say It

questions.question: Every probability must lie:
options: Between −1 and 1
Between 0 and 1 inclusive
Between 0 and 100 inclusive
Above 0,5

questions.question: The jar holds 14 blue, 10 white and 16 pink sweets. P(blue) as a decimal is:
The SAMPLE SPACE of an activity is:
options: The complete list of possible outcomes
The outcome you are hoping for
The number of trials carried out
The most likely outcome

questions.question: P(not blue) from the same jar is quickest to find by:
options: Counting the white and pink sweets one by one
Dividing 14 by 26
Taking 1 − 0,35 = 0,65, because an event and its complement add to 1
Doubling 0,35

questions.question: 93 of 150 counted taxis head for town. This 0,62 is an example of:
options: Theoretical probability, worked out by reasoning
A complementary event
An impossible event
Relative frequency, worked out from what actually happened

questions.question: Theoretical probability can only be used when:
options: All outcomes are equally likely
At least 100 trials have been recorded
The event has already happened
The answer is a whole percentage

questions.question: 27 heads in 60 tosses gives a relative frequency of 0,45. This shows that:
options: The coin is weighted towards tails
Small samples wander; larger samples settle towards the theoretical 0,5
The theoretical probability must actually be 0,45
Probability cannot be applied to coins

questions.question: After three heads in a row, the probability of heads on the next toss is:
options: Less than 0,5, because tails is due
More than 0,5, because heads is on a streak
0,5, because each toss is independent and the coin has no memory

subtopics.title: Two-Way Tables — Probability from Real Data

questions.question: Of 160 learners, 96 come by taxi. P(taxi) is:
64 learners are both under 16 AND come by taxi. P(under 16 and taxi) is:
"Of the learners under 16, what proportion come by taxi?" uses which denominator?
options: 160, the grand total
96, the number of taxi users
64, the cell value
100, the number of under-16s

questions.question: What should you check before using any two-way table?
options: That the row and column totals add to the grand total
That every cell is an even number
That the table has exactly four cells
That percentages have already been calculated

questions.question: Tossing two coins gives how many equally likely outcomes?
The rule for finding the probability of a two-stage path on a tree is to:
options: Add along the branches
Multiply along the branches
Divide the first stage by the second
Count the branches and halve them

questions.question: At R4,00 a turn with a R12,00 prize for two tails, over 100 turns the stall:
options: Breaks even exactly
Loses R100,00
Loses R300,00
Keeps R100,00 — R400,00 in against R300,00 out

questions.question: The prize that would make the two-coin game fair is:

subtopics.title: From Never to Always — Where Your Words Sit

questions.question: An answer of 1,2 for a probability tells you that:
options: The event is extremely likely
You have made a mistake, because no probability exceeds 1
The answer should be written as 120%
The event is certain

questions.question: 14 out of 40 written as a percentage is:
Which wording signals that you should reach for the complement?
options: "Both"
"Exactly two"
"In total"
"Not" or "at least one"

questions.question: Why can the taxi question NOT be answered by theory alone?
options: Because the destinations are not equally likely, so the answer has to be observed
Because taxis move too fast to count
Because theory only applies to coins and dice
Because 150 is too small a sample

questions.question: Of the 60 learners aged 16 and over, 32 come by taxi. That proportion is about:
The question to ask before writing any probability fraction is:
options: "Is it a percentage?"
"How many trials were there?"
"Out of whom?"
"Which number is bigger?"

questions.question: "The more you try, the closer the counting creeps to the thinking" describes:
options: The complement rule
Relative frequency approaching theoretical probability as trials increase
The belief that results even themselves out
The reason trees replace tables

questions.question: Why must HT and TH be listed separately?
options: Because heads is slightly more likely than tails
Because the tree would otherwise have three branches
Because the prize differs between them
Because they are different coins, so they are two different ways the toss can turn out

questions.question: The probability of one head and one tail (in any order) is:
options: 0,5, because two of the four outcomes give it

questions.question: A FAIR game is one in which:
options: Every player eventually wins something
Money in equals money out in the long run, so neither side expects to gain
The stall makes only a modest profit
The rules are displayed before you play

questions.question: The three questions to ask of any game of chance are:
options: Who runs it, how long is the queue, and is it popular
What does it cost, what fraction win, and what is the prize
Is it indoors, is it legal, and is it fun
How many coins, how many players, and how many prizes
